Anti-OX40L mAb. Ph3 ADHERE: ~47% IGA 0/1 at Wk24. Q12W dosing — best dosing interval in class. Phase 3 used treatment policy estimand (patients counted regardless of rescue med changes). If approved, becomes the OX40L monotherapy benchmark. Ailux IL-4Rα×OX40L aims to add IL-4Rα blockade + pH-extended half-life on top of the OX40L mechanism.

Anti-OX40 (receptor blocking, not ligand). ORIGIN Ph3 ongoing. Kaposi's sarcoma safety signal in predisposed patients. Mechanistically different from amlitelimab: receptor blocking more complete suppression vs. ligand blocking. If OX40 receptor blocking is too broad (safety), OX40L targeting is superior — directly validating Ailux approach.
AD, Asthma, EoE, CRSwNP, PN, COPD, CSU

Approved and market-defining in AD. Q2W dosing. 10–20% conjunctivitis in AD. IL-4Rα×OX40L bispecific targets post-dupilumab inadequate responders (~15–20% in trials) with a different mechanism (costimulatory + cytokine dual blockade).

Pure anti-IL-13. Q4W maintenance. Growing in market. Validates that patients exist who benefit from anti-IL-13 specifically (not just IL-4Rα blockade). Context: IL-4Rα×OX40L differs mechanistically — addresses T-cell priming (OX40L) + effector cytokines (IL-4Rα) rather than pure IL-13 pathway.
